shopify.text: Native. A market is a set of customers the merchant defines: countries or regions, company locations (B2B), retail locations or channels. The page states no per-plan market count.

criteria: A store lists the countries it sells to as markets, each with its own currency, default language, shipping rate, VAT rate and prices.
A market address is {country}[-{lang}][-{currency}] and a language or currency the store does not offer is not found.
A visitor's country is matched to the store's market for a suggestion; a country the store does not sell to gives none.
An owner can switch a product (or a variant) off in one market without deleting its price, and back on.
A product switched off in a market is absent from that market's listings, search, product page, chat, sitemap and structured data, and a cart line for it is refused.
The switch is read by cartSummary() and placeOrder() alike, and a checkout-kinds scenario (euro view included) holds that they agree.
A store copy (duplicate_store) carries the availability.

history.why: Wave 7 unit A (D335, docs/wave-7-storefront.md A.1, A.3): commerce.market_availability switches a product or a variant off in one market and back on, its price kept; commerce.current_prices leaves such a variant out, so listings, search, the product page (a 404 with no variant priced there), the sitemap, structured data and the chat's catalogue reads leave it out and the cart and placeOrder() refuse it, while the admin reads commerce.kept_prices. Set in the editor's Sold in box, the CSV's not_sold_in, the AI manager's not_sold_in and the bulk bar's Sell in / Stop selling in (with undo); copies carry it. market-availability.int.test.ts, a euro scenario in checkout-kinds.int.test.ts and e2e/signed-in/markets-in-depth.spec.ts hold it.

feature: Fixed per-market prices and adjustment rules
criteria: An owner sets a market rule (percentage up or down, rounding step) that derives that market's prices from a base price; a fixed price on a product overrides the rule.
Derived prices are written through commerce.set_price, so prior_30d_minor and the 30-day reference stay genuine.
A bulk change over a chosen set of products shows a preview (old and new price) before it is applied and is written to the audit log.
A euro-view scenario in checkout-kinds.int.test.ts holds that the shown price equals the charged price.

history.why: Wave 7 unit A2 (D335, docs/wave-7-storefront.md A.2): a market's prices can be worked out from another's by a standing rule (commerce.market_price_rules: percentage, before or with VAT, rounding step, ending), by the one BigInt sum derivedPrice() and written only through commerce.set_price with prices.derived, so the 30-day reference stays genuine; a price typed by hand is fixed and overrides the rule; prices follow a base price's save, a rule's save and the rates. Set on the Countries page with a five-product preview, or by the AI manager behind the owner's yes. market-prices.int.test.ts holds re-derivation, fixed prices, the reference and the store boundary; a checkout-kinds scenario holds a derived price shown in euro equal to the charge; e2e/signed-in/markets-in-depth.spec.ts sets a rule on the screen.

feature: EU withdrawal function and self-service returns

shopify.text: Native, partly. Shopify's page says merchants can use Shopify's return and cancellation rules to help meet the electronic withdrawal function requirement, and must set up the clearly labelled button or link, two-step confirmation and email confirmations themselves; Managed Markets orders get compliant policies automatically. No plan tiers are named. Apps also sell a withdrawal button.

history.why: D153 shipped the function: /withdraw in two steps with a confirmation (unconfirmed requests expire in 24 hours), the same reply for a wrong email or order number, an acknowledgement email on a durable medium (stored in email_messages, retried by the job), returns with a forward-only lifecycle, a staff queue and refund through refundOrder(), the 14-day clock from recorded receipt, and shopper status pages. Read the code and the integration, unit and e2e tests (returns*.int.test.ts, withdrawal.test.ts, e2e/withdrawal.spec.ts).

criteria: A shopper withdraws at /s/{store}/{market}/withdraw in two steps (Withdraw from contract here, then Confirm withdrawal) without giving a reason; nothing is a withdrawal until the second step, and an unconfirmed request expires after 24 hours.
The reply is the same for a wrong email, an unknown order number and another store's order, and requests are limited by hashed keys, never by IP.
Confirming records the statement, creates a return and sends an acknowledgement on a durable medium with date and time; a failed email never undoes the withdrawal and is retried.

Eligibility and the 14-day period come only from lineEligibility() and withdrawalWindow(); the period counts from a recorded receipt, never an estimate, and excluded goods, companies, digital content and copied orders are refused with a reason.

Staff work a queue (receive, inspect, refund through refundOrder()); the refund amount comes only from refundFor() and never exceeds what was captured; a withdrawal return is never declined or cancelled.
Known limits, stated in docs/returns.md and not counted here: texts need human legal review; no carrier return labels, exchanges, or photos (separate rows).

shopify.text: App. Shopify's own withdrawal page says nothing about exclusions or a digital-content waiver. Apps such as EU Withdrawal Form let merchants exclude items (hygiene, personalised) and the listing does not mention a digital waiver; community threads say the waiver checkbox needs checkout customisation, which Shopify Basic does not allow.

criteria: Each variant carries one of the statutory exclusions (custom made, perishable, sealed hygiene, sealed media, mixed inseparably, price fluctuation, alcohol for future delivery, periodicals, digital content, dated service) or none, and the product editor offers them.
A download is bought only after the shopper ticks the digital-content consent at checkout; the consent time is stored on the order and the lines become digital_content.
The withdrawal function refuses an excluded line with its reason (sealed goods keep the right until unsealed) and never refuses a line that has the right.

criteria: CI runs an automated WCAG check over the storefront's front, product, cart, order, account (signed out) and withdraw pages, the checkout in the states reachable without a payment session, and the admin's signed-out entry pages, in light and dark where the theme allows, and fails on serious or critical violations. The database refuses to activate a product that lacks these, and the editor says why before saving; downloads need none.

shopify.text: Native. Merchants enter a total measurement and optional base measure per product or variant; the unit price shows on product, collection, cart, checkout and order-confirmation notifications; Online Store 2.0 themes need no change. The page notes it is a legal requirement in some regions, that the unit type is the same across all markets, and that some units (t, cg, st) are not offered.

gap: Built and held by tests (D160, in production). A goods variant carries a measure, a unit and a base (`product_variants.measure_*`, database checks), `unitPrice()` (BigInt, half up, `src/lib/unit-price.ts`) is the only place a price is divided, and the figure follows the price as shown: the product page and its variant and plan choice, cards (the variant the card's price is of), cart and slide-out cart, checkout, order page, emails, chat cards and the subscription and weekly-delivery lists, with the business buyer's net price and the euro view's own figure (435 cents shown is 1740 per kg; converting the krone figure would say 1739), frozen on the order line (`order_lines.measure_*`, copied by `placeOrder()`, the renewal and `copy_orders()`), `priceSpecification` in the JSON-LD, and a deferred constraint trigger that refuses an active product without a measure under `sold_by_measure` or a marked category or ancestor. I ran these in my own database on 2026-10-04 after a fresh build: 20 unit files (355 tests), `unit-price.int.test.ts`, `checkout-kinds.int.test.ts` (every scenario runs `expectUnitPrices()`, euro included), `standing-orders.int.test.ts` (146 integration tests in all) and `e2e/unit-price.spec.ts` (8 of 8) passed. Still short of Full, by WAVES.md step 4: (1) the rules and words are unreviewed. The country table has no country that allows 100 g or 100 ml (Germany read in a PAngV mirror, Sweden's KOVFS 2012:1 6 § read on lagen.nu, Norway's FOR-2012-11-14-1066 read on lovdata.no on 2026-10-04, Denmark's BEK 1696/2017 never read and closed, flagged `verified: false`), so the criterion's "100 g and 100 ml where allowed" is a mechanism an owner cannot reach today and a test opens by a test helper; the rule that discounts, codes, campaigns, credits and reverse-charge relief leave a line's unit price alone, whether Directive Art. 6a wants a prior unit price (not read), the business buyer's net unit price, a multi-pack's total as the measure, the nb/sv/da/en words (Enhetspris, Jämförpris, Enhedspris) and the JSON-LD unit codes (from memory) all need a lawyer or a native speaker (spec section 8). (2) The owner's side (the editor's measure fields and the category and product flags) is held by server integration tests and render tests; nothing drives it in a browser because the e2e suite has no admin sign-in. (3) Checkout is held by `checkout-section.test.ts` and the integration scenarios, not by e2e (the page cannot be driven there). (4) The email line is held by one integration test (`unit-price.int.test.ts`), not a render test (the spec named `shopper-emails.test.ts`, which does not exist). (5) Orders placed before this unit carry no snapshot and show no unit price; the invoice document does not show the per-measure price. Merchant Center's `unit_pricing_measure` and `unit_pricing_base_measure` are now written by the product feed (D302, `src/lib/feeds.ts`, `feeds.test.ts`). (6) The migrations (`unit_price`, `unit_price_rules` and the `clone_store`, `duplicate_store` and `copy_orders` patches) are applied in production (checked 2026-10-14), but nothing about it was seen working there beyond that.
criteria: A variant can carry a total measure and unit (g, kg, ml, cl, l, cm, m, m2, piece) and a reference quantity (default 1 kg, 1 l, 1 m, 1 m2, 1 piece; 100 g or 100 ml only where a market's rule allows it: no country does today, so none).

The product page, listing cards (for the variant the card's price shows), cart, checkout (the pending order's page), order page and order emails show the unit price with the shown VAT treatment, converted per market currency like the price, and computed in code from the shown price.
A reduced price shows the unit price of the price charged; the unit price is never computed from, struck through against, or shown beside the 30-day reference price.

The product's JSON-LD offer carries a priceSpecification of type UnitPriceSpecification with price, priceCurrency and a referenceQuantity whose valueReference is the base measure, as Google's merchant listing documentation shows (the Merchant Center feed attributes unit_pricing_measure and unit_pricing_base_measure are produced by the feed row of wave 5 from the same data). A product the owner marked as sold by measure, or that is in a product category the owner marked as needing a unit price, cannot be saved active while an active physical variant has no measure; a draft can, an existing active product is reported rather than hidden, and the database refuses the same state.

A euro-view scenario in checkout-kinds.int.test.ts holds that the unit price shown equals the one computed from the charged price, defined as the order line's unit price (the listed price per unit; basket-level discounts are separate rows).

feature: Legal invoices and credit notes for orders
gap: Built and held by tests (unit 1b, D159, in production): the invoice and credit-note machinery of the two rows above, in the store's own gap-free series, with seller and buyer, VAT per rate, VAT number, payment and dates, the VAT in the seller's currency (`vatHome`) for an order in another currency (Art. 230), reverse charge with both numbers and the IOSS number, a PDF and a link in the emails, on the order page and on the hosted page, and the rules that copied and host orders get none and that numbers cannot be re-prefixed, lowered, skipped or removed (`invoices.test.ts`, `document_audit()` finds a hand-made gap). Euro views of every product kind, with a code, a group discount, a campaign, a gift and a delivery quote, are held in `checkout-kinds.int.test.ts` (invoice total and VAT per rate equal the order's, credit notes sum to the refunds and bring the VAT per rate to zero), and the reverse-charge and IOSS orders in `vat-engine.int.test.ts`. I ran these in my own database on 2026-10-04: all passed. Still short of Full: (1) the legal wording is unreviewed (spec section 8, ten items) and the content list is checked for NO, SE, DK, DE and the Directive only, from sources that were partly secondary or unreadable (EUR-Lex, gesetze-im-internet.de); nothing is claimed for any other member state; so by WAVES.md step 4 the row is not Full until an accountant or lawyer per country has read the real PDFs (spec 9.7); (2) a bonus-credit order, the criterion's own example, is held only by the fixture-based `invoice-parity.test.ts` (the SQL snapshot equals the pure oracle, with a bonus line and a welcome discount) and not by a checkout scenario: the D130 scenarios in `checkout-kinds.int.test.ts` do not call the document check; (3) the criterion's totals are the order's less free-trial subscription lines billed at the first renewal, and the notes sum to the refunds up to what the invoice left uncredited; a refund of a payment not on the invoice (a no-show fee) gets none; (4) the e2e is a fixture order, no Storage, no Chromium on Vercel, no real Stripe; the migrations are applied in production (checked 2026-10-14) but no document has been seen issued there; invoicing off for stores with history (see the invoice row); (5) not built: simplified invoices, exemption references, structured e-invoices (Germany's issuing mandate starts 2027 and 2028), and the per-measure unit price (D160) on the document itself. Since unit 1b, the VAT, OSS and IOSS reports (1c, D161) read these documents, erasure (1g, D162) anonymises them when the seller country's period ends, an order change issues its own invoice and edit credit note (D174, `commerce.issue_edit_documents()`), an exchange one `return_exchange` credit note (D239), an order on payment terms carries its due date (D293), and a gift card line is marked `voucher` (D300).
criteria: A paid shop order gets a legal invoice in the store's own gap-free series (seller and buyer details, VAT per rate, VAT number, payment, date) issued once by an SQL function and immutable afterwards, with a PDF and a link in the order email and account; legal means the content list for NO, SE, DK, DE and the VAT Directive's Art. 226, not another country's.
A refund or a withdrawal refund produces a credit note in its own gap-free series that references the invoice and lists the refunded lines and VAT.

Invoice and credit-note totals equal the order's less free-trial subscription lines billed at the first renewal, and the credit notes sum to the refunds up to what the invoice left uncredited (including bonus credit, group and code discounts, multi-currency), held by scenarios in checkout-kinds.int.test.ts.
Copied and host orders get none; the numbers cannot be skipped, lowered or deleted.
